{{Short description|Russian-American mathematician (born 1939)}}
{{Fnh|Borisovich|Fuchs|lang=Eastern Slavic}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2026}}
[[File:Dmitry Fuchs (cropped).jpg|thumb|Fuchs at [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]], 2006]]
'''Dmitry Borisovich Fuchs''' ({{langx|ru|Дмитрий Борисович Фукс|Dmitry Borisovich Fuks}},<ref>{{cite web |title=Персоналии: Фукс Дмитрий Борисович |url=http://www.mathnet.ru/php/person.phtml?option_lang=rus&personid=21985 |website=Math-Net.ru }}</ref> born 30 September 1939) is a Soviet and American mathematician, specializing in the representation theory of infinite-dimensional [[Lie group]]s and in topology.<ref>[http://www.math.ucdavis.edu/research/profiles/fuchs Dmitry B. Fuchs, Mathematics, University of California, Davis]</ref> He was born in  [[Kazan]], [[Soviet Tatarstan]].<ref>[http://dic.academic.ru/dic.nsf/enc_biography/30424/%D0%A4%D1%83%D0%BA%D1%81 Comprehensive Biographical Encyclopedia] {{in lang|ru}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Fuchs received in 1964 his Russian candidate degree (Ph.D.) under [[Albert S. Schwarz]] at [[Moscow State University]],<ref name=MG>{{MathGenealogy|id=14973|name=Dmitry Borisovich Fuchs}}</ref> where he taught thereafter. Schwarz conducted a seminar on algebraic topology with [[Mikhail Postnikov]] and [[Vladimir Boltyansky]]. Fuchs participated in the seminar and, as a student, published papers with  Schwarz, as did [[Askold Ivanovich Vinogradov]] a few years earlier. Fuchs received his Russian doctorate (higher doctoral degree) in 1987 at [[Tbilisi State University]]. Since 1991 he has been a professor at the [[University of California, Davis]].

With [[Israel Gelfand]] he introduced in 1970 the Gelfand-Fuchs cohomology of Lie algebras.<ref>Israel M. Gel'fand, Dmitry B. Fuks: ''Cohomologies of Lie algebra of tangential vector fields of a smooth manifold.'' In: ''Functional Analysis and its Applications.'' vol. 3, no. 3, 1969, pp. 194–210, {{doi|10.1007/BF01676621}}. Israel M. Gel'fand, Dmitry B. Fuks: ''Cohomology of the Lie algebra of formal vector fields.'' In: ''Mathematics of the USSR. Izvestija.'' vol. 4, no. 2, 1970, pp. 327–340, {{doi|10.1070/IM1970v004n02ABEH000908}}.</ref> Gelfand-Fuchs cohomology has applications in the proof of the [[Macdonald identities]] in combinatorics and in the calculation of characteristic classes of [[foliation]]s. With [[Boris Feigin]] he determined the structure of [[Verma module]]s in the [[Virasoro algebra]] representation theory, which has applications in [[string theory]] and [[conformal field theory]].<ref>with Fedor G. Malikov and Boris L. Feigin: ''Singular vectors in Verma modules over Kac—Moody algebras.'' In: ''Functional Analysis and its Applications.'' vol. 20, no. 2, 1986, pp. 103–113, {{doi|10.1007/BF01077264}}. Boris L. Feigin, Dmitry B. Fuchs: ''Representations of the Virasoro Algebra.'' In: Anatolii M. Vershik, Dmitrii P. Zhelobenko (eds.): ''Representation of Lie groups and related topics'' (= ''Advanced Studies in Contemporary Mathematics.'' vol. 7). Gordon and Breach, New York NY 1990, {{ISBN|2-88124-678-8}}, pp. 465–554.</ref>

His students include Boris Feigin (with whom he has collaborated extensively), Fedor Malikov, [[Sergei Tabachnikov]], and [[Vladimir Rokhlin Jr.|Vladimir Rokhlin]], as well as [[Edward Frenkel]] for whom Fuchs was a second advisor.<ref>Fuchs also lectured at the unofficial ''Jewish University'' in Moscow at the Institute for Petrochemical and Natural Gas Industry. {{cite journal|author=Saul, Mark|title=Kerosinka: An Episode in the History of Soviet Mathematics|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=46|issue=10|year=1999|issn=0002-9920|pages=1217–1220|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199910/fea-saul.pdf}}</ref> Frenkel, among many others, was affected by the Soviet antisemitism which flourished from 1954 to 1970 (described by Fuchs) and on into the 1980s.<ref>{{cite web|author=Fuchs, D. B.|title=On Soviet Mathematics of the 1950s and 1960s|url=http://math.uchicago.edu/~drinfeld/Golden%20years/Fuchs.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Edward Frenkel: Reality is a Paradox - Mathematics, Physics, Truth & Love {{!}} Lex Fridman Podcast #370|journal=Lex Fridman, YouTube|date=April 2023|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Osh0-J3T2nY&t=11790s}} (mention of Soviet antisemitism at 3:16:30 of 3:46:38 in video)</ref>

In 1978 Fuchs was an Invited Speaker with talk ''New results on the characteristic classes of foliations'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Helsinki]].

==Personal life==
Fuchs's father was also a mathematician, and a student of [[Stefan Bergman]].<ref name="q182">{{cite book |last=Fuchs |first=D. B. |editor-last1=Zdravkovska | editor-first1=Smilka | editor-last2=Duren | editor-first2=Peter L. | title=Golden Years of Moscow Mathematics | publisher=American Mathematical Soc. | publication-place=Washington D.C. | date=2007 | isbn=978-0-8218-4261-4 | chapter=On Soviet Mathematics of the 1950s and 1960s}}</ref>
His daughter Elena Fuchs is also a professor in the mathematics department at UC Davis, and his daughter Ekaterina Fuchs is a professor in the mathematics department at the [[City College of San Francisco]].<ref name="w790">{{cite journal | last1=Fialowski | first1=Alice | last2=Fuchs | first2=Ekaterina | last3=Fuchs | first3=Elena | last4=Khesin | first4=Boris | last5=Kirillov | first5=Alexandre | last6=Malikov | first6=Fedor | last7=Ovsienko | first7=Valentin | last8=Sossinsky | first8=Alexei | last9=Tabachnikov | first9=Serge | title=On the 80th Birthday of Dmitry Borisovich Fuchs | journal=Symmetry, Integrability and Geometry: Methods and Applications | date=2020-04-07 | doi=10.3842/SIGMA.2020.023 | url=https://sigma-journal.com/2020/023/ | arxiv=2004.03270 }}</ref><ref name="d659">{{cite web | title=General Profile :: math.ucdavis.edu | website=Mathematics Home | date=2016-01-01 | url=https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/people/general-profile?fac_id=efuchs }}</ref><ref name="v699">{{cite web | title=Katia Fuchs | website=CCSF | url=https://www.ccsf.edu/directory/katia-fuchs }}</ref>
